key_insight: Replacing Cr with Cu in MnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys substantially improves bifunctional alkaline water-splitting activity by tuning surface chemistry and intermediate binding.
engineering_relevance: A single-element substitution in HEAs can be used as a practical design lever to develop more efficient, lower-cost electrocatalysts for hydrogen production.
method: Compared CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) and MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) under the same alkaline HER/OER conditions.
Combined electrochemical testing with computational electronic-structure analysis of reaction-intermediate binding.
Examined post-OER surface evolution to assess Cu redistribution and shell formation.
evidence_signal: HEA-Cu showed better HER and OER performance than HEA-Cr, including a lower overpotential of 538 mV and a Tafel slope of 165 mV dec-1, consistent with computed favorable binding energies for H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*.
watch_item: The reported Cu migration and Cu-rich shell after OER suggests that long-term stability and surface reconstruction must be considered before deployment.
paper_title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
